Nina (Presales): Heads-up: Novellus wants a 72h POC next month. Scope: streaming recommendations, an `issue_refund` function-call that posts to their order service, and guaranteed structured JSON for downstream analytics. They asked about ephemeral creds, proxy behavior, and a quick pricing estimate.
Arjun (Eng): Minimal handshake: 1) ephemeral token (TTL 10m) from our token endpoint, 2) ability to accept HMAC-signed webhook calls, 3) sample client for SSE and WS. If their proxy strips Authorization on upgrade we fall back to signed query param.
Bea (SDK): I'll prep Node and Go quickstarts. Node snippet for SSE client: `const client = new Redwood({token: process.env.POC_TOKEN}); client.stream({model:'rec-lite', onEvent: e => console.log(e)});` Also adding `registerTool('issue_refund', handler)` example and a validate-with-ajv snippet for the order schema.
Kai (Security): For the POC: redact PII in samples, only hashed user ids in telemetry, ephemeral tokens server-side. We'll provide SOC2 packet; note that KMS-backed key ops require Private deployment and a short addendum. Retention for POC logs: 7 days.
Nina (Presales): Pricing: they asked "ballpark cost for 60 concurrent shoppers with bursts to 300 QPS" — need a short slide.
Arjun (Eng): Back-of-envelope: with batching/prefix cache expect ~0.6-1.1 tokens/sec per active connection; sustained burst capacity suggests recommending Dedicated pilot. I'll put numbers in a spreadsheet and include a sample cost table per-hour.
Bea (SDK): Fallback curl to mint ephemeral token: `curl -X POST https://auth.redwood.ai/v1/ephemeral -H 'Authorization: Bearer <svc>' -d '{"role":"novellus-poc","ttl":600}'` I'll attach the schema JSON and a small express webhook consumer in the repo.
deploy-bot: demo branch `poc/novellus` deployed to staging (build 2026.18345) :rocket:
Nina (Presales): Great. Action items: Bea -> quickstarts + schema + HMAC fallback; Arjun -> runbook + allowlist steps; Kai -> security packet + redaction checklist. Sync in 45m.
